result.defense: C is the best weighted balance: it removes the 576px-wide scrolling section strip entirely, so at rest only the unclipped 'Usage' menu button shows and one tap reveals all 7 sections fully labelled vertically (Files through Activity & deletion, with Usage as the dark selected bay), and content starts at y=159, well under 260. A fails the hard acceptance gate despite being cheapest: its screenshot still shows 'Activ...' cut at rest and 'Research worksp...' ellipsized, so labels are clipped and Activity & deletion requires swipe-hunting with only a fade as cue. B measurably meets every criterion best (content y=134, full-width drive switcher, 5 bottom tabs plus More sheet for Billing & limits and Activity & deletion), but it invents a global fixed bottom bar that departs from the Rack top-nav system, must be rolled out to billing/settings pages to stay consistent, and buries two sections under More — a large, risky restructure to gain only 25px over C, which already passes y<=260 comfortably. C keeps the light-grey top chassis and familiar drive strip logic at medium effort, follows proven Vercel/GitHub/Linear mobile convention, and its one residual weakness — possible drive-name truncation from the retained strip — is fixed by the single B graft without importing B's bottom-bar overhaul.

result.defense: Proposal C wins because collapsing the section navigation into a top-bar dropdown button ('Usage ▾') alongside the compact 'a/' mark and user avatar reclaims over 160px of vertical space (content at y=159 vs y=260 target) while presenting all 7 sections vertically with full labels, icons, badge counts, and a logical divider above Billing and Activity. Against Proposal A, C eliminates the mobile anti-pattern of stacking two horizontal scroll strips on top of each other; in A, off-screen sections ('Files', 'Agents') remain hidden to the left, 'Activity & deletion' is still visibly clipped to 'Activ...' at rest, and the dual edge-fade masks look muddy. Against Proposal B, C avoids an overcrowded 6-item bottom tab bar (exceeding the 5-tab mobile ergonomics limit), avoids hiding two sections behind an extra 'More' sheet tap, preserves the T1 'Rack' developer console aesthetic instead of introducing a consumer-style white bottom sheet, and requires only localized header changes rather than high-risk cross-page layout restructuring.
